neutral_facts.value: The accused, the husband of the deceased, was charged with abetment of suicide and cruelty under the Indian Penal Code. The deceased died from severe burn injuries shortly after her marriage. The prosecution alleged that the accused demanded money from her father-in-law, which led to the deceased taking extreme measures by pouring kerosene on herself and setting herself on fire. Evidence included the recovery of kerosene at the scene, statements from witnesses about the accused's behavior, and the pledging of the deceased's jewels. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court reversed this decision, finding the prosecution's case credible. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision, concluding that the deceased's suicide was instigated by the accused due to the cruelty and financial demands.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the consistent statements of PWs 3, 9, and 11, the recoveries made at the place of occurrence (kerosene cane, piece of cloth soaked in kerosene, quilt and pillows, clothes worn by the deceased with kerosene smell), the postmortem report, and the evidence of the postmortem doctor P.W.15.

quotes.text: The evidence of P.Ws.3, 9 and 11 amply disclosed that within few days after the marriage the appellant made a demand for a sum of Rs.40,000/-, that the non-payment of the said money to the appellant and the subsequent pledging of the jewels of the deceased which was established by Exhibit 7 as well as evidence of P.W.17 showed that the demand of dowry was amply established.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their consistent statements about the appellant's conduct and the deceased's grievances were supported by evidence and that there was no indication of ulterior motives.

quotes.text: No inconsistency was found in the evidence of P.W.3 and other witnesses who had the advantage of hearing from the mouth of the deceased about the conduct of the appellant relating to his demand, as well as, his illicit intimacy with the second accused.

other_sentence_order.value: The appellant was sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to suffer further one year rigorous imprisonment for the offence under Section 306 of IPC. He was also sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years apart from a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to suffer further rigorous imprisonment for one year for the offence under Section 498A of IPC. Both sentences were directed to run consecutively.
